subject: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline
thread_body:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Jordan / Lauren / Evelyn —

I’m pulling together NA enablement for the Dedicated Throughput Tiers rollout (Standard / Performance / Premium). A few asks so we can land this cleanly with reps and not create comp/quota confusion:

1) Timeline / “what’s sellable when”
- Are we treating this as internal beta -> controlled pilot -> broader availability? If yes, can we lock dates by tier (especially Premium due to H100 availability)?

2) Quota + comp signaling
- Do we position this as packaging change only (no quota credit change), or are we introducing a new SKU / uplift motion that needs explicit guidance?
- If we’re expecting higher ACVs, I’d like to be explicit about when/where uplifts are required vs exception-able.

3) Pilot accounts (NA)
Proposed pilot list based on active Dedicated conversations + pain around predictability:
- Northpeak AI (HubSpot 10482) — asking for explicit tokens/sec + burst semantics; currently in technical deep dive.
- Helio Search (HubSpot 10511) — procurement/legal focused on SLA language + auditability.
- (2–3) additional: I can nominate from pipeline this week, but want your view on “ideal pilot profile” (model size, region constraints, appetite for beta language).

I attached:
- dedicated-tier-launch-deck-draft.pptx (rough cut: why tiers, what changes, how to qualify)
- dedicated-throughput-tiers-cheatsheet.pdf (v0; needs final wording on guarantees + carve-outs)

If we align by EOD Monday, I can schedule a 30-min enablement for NA AE/SE early next week and ship the cheat sheet + FAQ.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Enablement Lead (NA)
Redwood Inference


---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Stephanie —

This is exactly the right set of questions.

On timeline/sellability (proposed):
- Standard + Performance: OK to “sell” as of internal announcement (targeting Tue 3/4), but with explicit language that regional shape availability may constrain start date.
- Premium: pilot-only initially; we should limit it to a short list due to H100 supply + extra SRE scrutiny on burst behavior.

Pilot profile guidance:
- Teams already experiencing pain with variance (mixed prompt sizes / peak hour spikes).
- Willing to share prompt length distribution + concurrency assumptions (so we can validate tier fit).
- Preferably 1 customer per: (a) latency-sensitive interactive, (b) batch-ish but steady throughput, (c) mixed streaming/non-streaming.

Northpeak and Helio both fit. I’d add one “fast-growing SaaS” account that wants predictable throughput but isn’t procurement-heavy, so we can test the sales motion without legal cycles.

Cheat sheet: we need to be extremely consistent about what is and isn’t guaranteed. I’ll review the v0 and send edits today.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated


---

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 1:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Agree with Lauren.

On quota/comp: we should treat this as a packaging improvement (i.e., no comp plan change), but we DO need clear pricing guardrails so reps don’t “give away” Premium semantics at Performance pricing.

My guidance for enablement:
- “Tier” is the commercial wrapper for an operational guarantee; it’s not a menu of custom SLAs.
- Exceptions (higher throughput target, expanded burst) require: (1) approval, (2) pricing uplift, (3) explicit carve-outs.

Evelyn — confirming: we’ll message internally as “available now” for Standard/Performance with regional constraints, and “pilot” for Premium?

Stephanie: for NA pilot list, I’d like 5 accounts total maximum in March to avoid swamping SRE/Infra. Northpeak + Helio are good. Please propose 3 more Monday.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
GTM Sponsor
Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, Mar 1, 2025 at 2:04 PM PT
Subject: Re: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Yes — that’s the message.

Two notes to bake into enablement:
1) We should NOT imply “unlimited burst” or “always-on max throughput.” The tier is a measurable guarantee with an overload behavior. If a customer wants different behavior, it’s an exception and should be treated as such.
2) Please keep “Premium” positioning tight: it’s for the customers who truly need it (and will pay for it). If we over-sell it, we’ll create supply and reliability issues.

Stephanie — approve moving forward with the NA enablement session early next week.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Executive Sponsor
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, Mar 2, 2025 at 10:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Thanks all.

I’ll update the enablement materials to reflect:
- Standard/Performance: “sellable now” with region/shape constraints; guarantees measured per the published measurement standard; clear exclusions.
- Premium: pilot-only; explicit approval + pricing uplift; limited account count.

Pilot list (proposed adds):
- Northpeak AI — interactive + streaming; asks are very aligned to the new semantics.
- Helio Search — procurement/legal heavy; good test for contract language + remedies.
- Calder Systems — SaaS; wants predictable throughput for in-app copilots; not procurement-heavy (good “sales motion” test).
- Ridgeview HealthTech — regulated-ish workload; wants Dedicated for isolation and predictability; will stress our “measurement + reporting” story.
- HorizonCX — contact center; peak hour spikes + mixed prompt sizes; good stress test for burst policy + overload behavior messaging.

If you’d prefer different profiles, I can swap, but this should give us breadth without being too many.

Next steps from me:
- Book 30-min NA enablement Tue or Wed.
- Ship updated cheat sheet + talk track same day.

Lauren — if you can send edits on the cheat sheet wording (guarantee vs throttling vs breach) by Monday morning, I’ll incorporate.

Stephanie

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 9:41 AM PT
Subject: Re: Launch enablement + quotas: Dedicated Throughput Tiers (NA) — pilot accounts + timeline

Pilot list looks good.

Cheat sheet edits (high-level) — please incorporate:
- Replace “throughput guarantee” with “throughput SLO” everywhere except the one approved external line (we can keep “guarantee” in the customer-facing one-pager but only alongside the measurement reference).
- Add one crisp example under each tier:
  - “If you exceed burst limits, you may see throttling (429/overload) — this is expected behavior, not an SLO breach.”
  - “If you are under the sustained SLO under defined conditions, that is an SLO miss and triggers our escalation/remedy path.”
- Put the top 3 qualifying questions at the top:
  1) Region + preferred shape constraints
  2) Expected concurrency + prompt length distribution
  3) Streaming vs non-streaming mix

Also: please avoid quoting specific tokens/sec numbers in the enablement deck until the tier definition page is published (we had one last-minute adjustment from SRE on the safety factor). We can tell reps where to find the canonical table and how to talk about it.

Lauren

- Q&A (5 min)

I’ll send the updated deck + cheat sheet right after Lauren confirms the tier page is live, and I’ll include a short “what to copy/paste” blurb for outbound and proposals.

Jordan — any additional guidance you want included on discounting language (beyond “Premium requires uplift + approval”)?

Stephanie
